Polygalaceae.key_door: 5 sepals with 2 enlarged petaloid wing sepals + keel petal + usually 8 united stamens + superior usually 2-locular ovary → flattened capsule

anchor_families.Fabaceae: papilionoid Fabaceae uses petal banner/wings/keel and a single-carpel legume; Polygalaceae's lateral 'wings' are sepals and its project fruit is a 2-locular capsule

taxonomy_notes: Polygala alba is a synonym of accepted Senega alba under the current Kew backbone.
Polygala lindheimeri is a homotypic synonym of accepted Rhinotropis lindheimeri.
Polygala lindheimeri var. lindheimeri maps to accepted Rhinotropis lindheimeri var. lindheimeri.
Senega lutea is accepted by current Kew; its Kew native range is eastern U.S., so any local encounter/range role remains species-lane work.
The source pool has three genus labels, but the current family lesson uses two accepted genera: Senega and Rhinotropis.
guardrails: Family/genus recognition only; no species promotion.
Do not call the enlarged lateral wing structures petals; they are inner sepals.
Do not double-count the source Rhinotropis lindheimeri species row and var. lindheimeri as two species.
Use Flora of North America descriptions for morphology while keeping the current Kew genus names explicit.
